summary: Guidance requested: split refill windows for background telemetry pulses vs interactive realtime streams
description: Customer runs a mixed workload in production: interactive realtime chat sessions (low tokens, high concurrency) and frequent background telemetry/heartbeat pings from a fleet of edge agents. Over the last week they started seeing a rising number of 429s that correlate with telemetry sweep windows. They want concrete guidance on whether to: 1) split refill windows (separate burst pools) for telemetry vs interactive lanes, 2) use separate API keys/routes for telemetry, or 3) tune smoothing/refill intervals to avoid synchronized tenant-level throttles.
impact: ~12% of interactive chat requests returned 429s during nightly telemetry sweeps; several customer-facing flows degrade (timeouts, retries). Affects production us-west region only. Billing unaffected but user experience degraded.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy 1000 edge agents configured to send telemetry heartbeat (small POST) every 60 seconds. 2) Start 200 concurrent interactive chat sessions that send occasional messages (avg 30 tokens) over WebSocket/HTTP3. 3) Observe token usage and 429 spikes in request timeline around minute boundaries when many heartbeats align. 4) Toggle telemetry heartbeat jitter and re-run to see effect.
logs: Sample throttle header from client: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 25s. Platform logs show tenant_token_window_exhausted events at 2026-03-09T03:00:00Z and 2026-03-10T03:00:00Z. Ingress traces show many short lived HTTP/3 connections from telemetry agents and long-lived websocket-like streams for chat. No 5xx accompanying errors.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: telemetry heartbeats are concentrated on the same refill epoch and are counted against the tenant-wide refill window used by interactive requests. HTTP/3 multipath and short connections may be causing preflight-like counting or connection-level aggregation anomalies. Possible contributing factors: (a) telemetry uses same API key/route and is not isolated, (b) refill interval (60s epoch) aligns with heartbeat cadence resulting in sawtooth token consumption, (c) smoothing parameters not tuned for high-cardinality short requests.
proposed_workaround: 1) Recommend separating telemetry onto a dedicated API key and route that maps to a distinct burst pool (isolated burst lane) so background pings cannot exhaust interactive quota. 2) If separate key not possible, add jitter to heartbeat schedule to desynchronize pulses. 3) Temporarily increase tenant burst credits during sweep windows or configure a short-lived exception for telemetry route via Console as a stopgap.
resolution_notes: Triage stage. Guidance prepared for customer; engineering inboxed to evaluate adding a Console UI path to create isolated burst pools for routes. If customer agrees, support will schedule a config change: create dedicated route + API key for telemetry and update docs with recommended jitter parameters. No code changes required immediately.
